tagline: The Caribbean's best-preserved walled city wraps colonial plazas in bougainvillea, minutes from white-sand islands and Colombia's salsa-coast nightlife.
overview: Founded in 1533, Cartagena grew rich as the main Spanish port for Peruvian gold — and rich enough to be raided by pirates, which is why 11 kilometres of walls and the giant San Felipe fortress still ring it. The walled Old Town is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

Inside the walls, every street is a postcard: pastel mansions, flower-draped balconies, horse-drawn carriages and plazas where palenqueras sell fruit in bright dresses. The fortress of San Felipe de Barajas, the largest Spanish fort in South America, guards the bay.

Getsemaní, the former working-class quarter, is now the city's street-art and nightlife heart. Offshore, the Rosario Islands offer day-trip beaches and snorkelling, and evenings belong to salsa clubs, sunset cocktails on the wall, and Gabriel García Márquez's city of magic realism.

funFacts.title: PIRATE-PROOF
funFacts.text: The walls and fortress took over 200 years to build after repeated attacks by pirates, including Francis Drake.

funFacts.title: THE LARGEST SPANISH FORT
funFacts.text: San Felipe de Barajas is the biggest colonial military fortress Spain ever built in the Americas.

funFacts.title: GABO'S CITY
funFacts.text: Gabriel García Márquez set novels here and kept a house in the Old Town — magic realism in real life.

funFacts.title: THE PALENQUERAS
funFacts.text: The fruit sellers in bright dresses descend from San Basilio de Palenque, the Americas' first free African town.

funFacts.title: WALLS YOU CAN WALK
funFacts.text: The 11-kilometre city wall is intact enough to stroll — Café del Mar sits on top of it at sunset.

funFacts.title: AN ISLAND ESCAPE
funFacts.text: The Rosario Islands' coral park is an hour offshore by boat.

funFacts.title: A CONVENT TURNED HOTEL
funFacts.text: The Sofitel Santa Clara was a 17th-century convent with crypts still beneath the bar.

funFacts.title: THE CLOCK TOWER
funFacts.text: The Torre del Reloj, built in 1601, is the city's symbol and the old walled city's gateway.

funFacts.title: EMERALD MARKETS
funFacts.text: Cartagena is a centre for Colombian emeralds — some of the finest in the world.

funFacts.title: A SUNKEN TREASURE
funFacts.text: The Spanish galleon San José, sunk in 1708 with treasure worth billions, lies off the coast.
